segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Welcome to Psalm Nights. [pause 8]

Let your body settle. There is nothing left to do today. [pause 11]

Tonight's psalm is Psalm 62. David wrote it when people were trying to pull him down. And yet the psalm is quiet. It is about waiting, and about a rock that does not move. [pause 10]

We will read it twice. [pause 13]

verses.text: To the chief Musician, to Jeduthun, A Psalm of David. Truly my soul waiteth upon God: from him cometh my salvation.
He only is my rock and my salvation; he is my defence; I shall not be greatly moved.
How long will ye imagine mischief against a man? ye shall be slain all of you: as a bowing wall shall ye be, and as a tottering fence.
They only consult to cast him down from his excellency: they delight in lies: they bless with their mouth, but they curse inwardly. Selah.
My soul, wait thou only upon God; for my expectation is from him.
He only is my rock and my salvation: he is my defence; I shall not be moved.
In God is my salvation and my glory: the rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God.
Trust in him at all times; ye people, pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us. Selah.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Truly my soul waiteth upon God. In older words, my soul is silent before God. Not anxious. Not rushing. Waiting. [pause 11]

Three times the psalm calls God a rock. A rock is not quick. It does not change its mind. You can lean your whole weight on it and it stays. [pause 11]

Then a line to say in your heart. Trust him at all times. Pour out your heart before him. [pause 11]

You can pour it out tonight. All of it. The worry, the hurt, the thing you did not say. He can hold it. [pause 15]

A companion passage from Isaiah. [pause 9]

verses.text: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.
Trust ye in the LORD for ever: for in the LORD JEHOVAH is everlasting strength:
The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my strength, in whom I will trust; my buckler, and the horn of my salvation, and my high tower.
Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Everlasting strength. A rock of ages. The same picture, in another book, centuries apart. [pause 11]

Psalm 18 piles up the same pictures. Rock, fortress, deliverer, shield, high tower. And Jesus, in the gospel, says come to me, and I will give you rest. [pause 13]

Here is Psalm 62 again. Let your soul wait as you listen. [pause 15]

verses.text: To the chief Musician, to Jeduthun, A Psalm of David. Truly my soul waiteth upon God: from him cometh my salvation.
He only is my rock and my salvation; he is my defence; I shall not be greatly moved.
How long will ye imagine mischief against a man? ye shall be slain all of you: as a bowing wall shall ye be, and as a tottering fence.
They only consult to cast him down from his excellency: they delight in lies: they bless with their mouth, but they curse inwardly. Selah.
My soul, wait thou only upon God; for my expectation is from him.
He only is my rock and my salvation: he is my defence; I shall not be moved.
In God is my salvation and my glory: the rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God.
Trust in him at all times; ye people, pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us. Selah.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
That is enough for tonight. [pause 8]

Let your breathing slow down on its own. In, and out. Nothing to fix, nothing to finish. [pause 12]

Whatever today was, it is over now. Tomorrow has not come yet. This is only the night, and the night belongs to God. [pause 12]

Lay down what you carried. One thing, and then another. [pause 15]

Stay here as long as you like. [pause 15]

If your mind wanders, let it wander back. There is no wrong way to rest. [pause 20]

The Lord is near. Nearer than your breath. [pause 20]

Good night. [pause 45]

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Every psalm and companion is stored KJV pasted by code; reflections paraphrase in short echoes (no 8+ word typed scripture) and stay with each psalm's own point (shepherd, evening rest, keeping, shelter, stillness, quiet soul, being known, waiting, a shield in flight, light and waiting). No promise of sleep or protection: Psalm 91 says plainly it does not promise nothing hard will happen; Proverbs 3:24 framed as 'not a promise for every night'. God never quoted in first person outside scripture. Headings (Ps 3, Absalom) used only as the text's own titles.

cultural.note: Plain, unhurried English a tired woman at 11 PM can follow; no filler, no church jargon unexplained; hospital and grief named gently; shared rests vary their wording so the close is not the same sentence every night; pacing tuned only by silence (pauses) to 13.6-15.3 minutes.
